value.first: At 6 months he's right on time. I'd go with iron-first solids and early allergens: start about now, never before 4 months. Why: iron stores run low around 6 months, and the LEAP trial found roughly 80% less peanut allergy in high-risk babies who ate it early and regularly. Day 1: upright in a high chair, rested, a spoon or two of iron-fortified oat cereal, puréed beef or mashed lentils. Most lands on the tray, and that's a win. Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, with veg and fruit alongside. Milk stays as usual.
value.second: Allergens, from week 2, one new one per day, in the morning, with no other new foods that day. Peanut first: half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter thinned with warm water or breast milk. Never a glob, never whole nuts. Give a tiny taste, wait about 10 minutes, feed the rest, and keep him in sight for two hours. Next day or two: well-cooked egg. Then yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, thinned nut butters, flaked fish. No allergy testing is needed first. Once a food is tolerated, keep it about twice a week, since dropping it can undo the protection.
value.third: Gagging is normal: it's noisy and red-faced, and fades with practice. Choking is silent. Mess is the method. No honey before 12 months, no cow milk as a drink yet. A few hives or vomiting tied to one food: stop it and see your doctor first. Eczema or a known allergy: talk to your doctor before the allergens. I'll check in Friday. Emma Hubbard, a paediatric OT, has a good starting-solids guide if you want to watch it done.
